question.text: A tower $T_1$ of height $60 \mathrm{~m}$ is located exactly opposite to a tower $T_2$ of height $80 \mathrm{~m}$ on a straight road. From the top of $T_1$, if the angle of depression of the foot of $T_2$ is twice the angle of elevation of the top of $T_2$, then the width (in $m$ ) of the road between the feet of the towers $T_1$ and $T_2$ is

solution.text:
$$ \text { Let the distance between } T_1 \text { and } T_2 \text { be } x $$
From the figure $E A=60 \mathrm{~m}\left(T_1\right)$ and $D B=80 \mathrm{~m}\left(T_2\right)$ $\angle D E C=\theta$ and $\angle B E C=2 \theta$ Now in $\triangle D E C$, $$ \tan \theta=\frac{D C}{A B}=\frac{20}{x} $$ and in $\triangle B E C$, $$ \tan 2 \theta=\frac{B C}{C E}=\frac{60}{x} $$ We know that $$ \tan 2 \theta=\frac{2 \tan \theta}{1-(\tan \theta)^2} $$ $$ \begin{aligned} &\Rightarrow \frac{60}{x}=\frac{2\left(\frac{20}{x}\right)}{1-\left(\frac{20}{x}\right)^2} \\ &\Rightarrow x^2=1200 \Rightarrow x=20 \sqrt{3} \end{aligned} $$
